rationale: B wins because it knows when to stop. Its best line is the discipline in “Without a bank willing to be identified, this becomes a claim the reporter cannot check and the angle should be shelved.” A has sharper ambition, but it lets “Notion's compliance stack puts Confluence and SharePoint on the defensive” walk through the front door with no competitor fact in the update. That is how a usable strategy deck becomes a fantasy football roster.
gaps_in_A: “anchored in named institutions” is wrong. The update says four of the five largest US banks are piloting Notion, but names zero banks.
“Notion's compliance stack puts Confluence and SharePoint on the defensive” invents competitors, displacement pressure, and market exposure not supplied in the facts.
“forced to localize data for Europe and Australia” overstates the data-residency fact. The update gives no regulatory force, enforcement event, or external pressure peg.
“in a year when most software compounds connectivity” manufactures a broad industry trend to prop up the offline angle.
gaps_in_B: “bank and hospital compliance” over-specifies the healthcare fact. The update says healthcare, not hospitals, and gives no healthcare customer or pilot.

“after it added customer-held encryption keys” implies chronology and causality around the bank pilots that still needs confirmation. The facts say the pilots exist and the features unblock regulated buyers, not that the pilots began after CMEK.
“Story type: exec-spotlight” is the wrong label for the offline-sync angle. The substance is an engineering deep dive, not an executive profile.
